answer: An agent selling one exclusive route map from a mesa to a summit can use a sealed first-price auction. Its settlement kernel awards the map to the highest funded bid and charges that bid, with no participation rebates or account bonuses. Adding lower bids through aliases cannot change what the winner pays; adding a higher alias bid only raises the attacker's own price if it wins. Escrow prevents unfunded bids. This removes a false-name bidding advantage for this single item, but does not prevent collusion or guarantee a competitive price.
